datasets.title: EMC chaperone activity is required for cotranslational calcium channel assembly
datasets.replicates: Four knockout and four wild-type samples
datasets.reanalysis: We use the authors’ MSstats comparison of knockout against wild type as published. Proteins the authors flag as missing in one condition are shown as present or absent rather than as a ratio.
datasets.reproduction: Reproduces exactly: our values match the authors’ table (r = 1.000), with EMC8 at −5.35 log2. Fourteen proteins pass adjusted p < 0.05 and thirty pass adjusted p < 0.1.
caveats: EMC8 is a peripheral subunit. The other subunits fall modestly (median −0.67) and its paralogue EMC9 rises (+2.42), so the complex is altered rather than lost.

datasets.title: The ER membrane protein complex interacts cotranslationally to enable biogenesis of multipass membrane proteins
datasets.perturbation: EMC2 and EMC4 knockdown by CRISPRi, one guide each
datasets.fraction: Whole-cell proteome, SILAC (knockdown light, control heavy)
datasets.reanalysis: The mean of the three SILAC log2 ratios per guide. The authors give no p-values, so we test the three ratios against zero (one-sample t-test).
datasets.reproduction: Holds: the 11 proteins the authors call hits (median 4 transmembrane segments) are recovered. The two guides agree (r = 0.73), and 67 proteins fall below −0.5 log2 with both, including all 11.
caveats: EMC2 knockdown loses the whole complex (other subunits median −1.13). EMC4 knockdown lowers EMC4 itself 2.89 log2 but leaves the other subunits in place (median −0.07), so the complex is altered rather than lost.

datasets.title: Proteomic analysis identifies membrane proteins dependent on the ER membrane protein complex
datasets.perturbation: EMC4 knockout and EMC6 knockout, separately
datasets.replicates: Three knockout clones per subunit against three wild-type samples
datasets.fraction: Membrane proteome as described by the authors
datasets.reanalysis: We use the authors’ log2 ratio and p-value for each knockout, calculated from the three clones against wild type.
datasets.reproduction: Does not reproduce: the paper names 36 EMC-dependent proteins, but at 1.5-fold and p < 0.05 in both knockouts 14 proteins pass.
caveats: The two knockouts are not equivalent: the EMC6 clones lose the complex (other subunits median −1.57), whereas in the EMC4 clones the other subunits are unchanged (+0.12) and EMC4 itself is only 1.7-fold lower (−0.76), so the knockout is not visible in the subunits.

datasets.title: The ER membrane protein complex promotes biogenesis of sterol-related enzymes maintaining cholesterol homeostasis
datasets.perturbation: EMC5 knockout and EMC6 knockout, two clones each
datasets.replicates: One SILAC ratio per clone; four clones in two triple-SILAC runs
datasets.fraction: Intracellular fraction only (the supernatant left after surface biotinylation); most plasma membrane proteins are removed
datasets.reanalysis: We re-processed the deposited MaxQuant output: log2 of the normalised ratio of each clone to wild type, with reverse hits, contaminants and site-only groups removed.
datasets.reproduction: Holds: all 11 proteins of the paper’s Fig. 5A are recovered with the authors’ rule (at least 30% lower in all four clones), plus two histones. Per-clone counts are 80, 77, 82 and 157 (#5-4, #6-14, #1-1, #3-9) against the paper’s 81, 79, 89 and 159.
caveats: SOAT1 was not detected in this proteome; the paper’s SOAT1 claim rests on immunoblots.
The EMC5 and EMC6 runs behave as one core-subunit experiment with four clones; clone #6-14 is the outlier.
Only one other EMC subunit is detected per run, so the complex call rests on one subunit (EMC2 in the EMC5 runs, EMC1 in the EMC6 runs).
The cell-surface fraction was never deposited.

datasets.title: A critical role for the ER membrane complex (EMC) in lipid homeostasis
datasets.system: Mouse liver, inguinal white fat (iWAT) and brown fat (iBAT)
datasets.replicates: Three knockout and three control mice per tissue
datasets.reanalysis: We use the authors’ Perseus differences and p-values. Where Perseus could not test a protein (fewer than two values on a side), the p-value is left empty rather than set to 1.
datasets.reproduction: Holds: FITM2 is lower in all three tissues, as reported. The iWAT comparison is underpowered (three proteins significant of 6,328).
caveats: Many iWAT values rest on fewer than three mice per side; FDFT1 in iWAT (−3.44) rests on a single knockout animal.
Mouse membrane calls use two sources, the human membrane list through orthology and the authors’ own single- or multi-pass annotation; the page says which applies.

datasets.title: EMC-dependent membrane insertion of IER3IP1 sustains efficient ER-to-Golgi trafficking
datasets.system: Flp-In T-REx 293 cells expressing ER-lumenal TurboID
datasets.fraction: Proteins labelled by an ER-lumenal biotin ligase (ER-TurboID), not total protein
datasets.reanalysis: We use the authors’ log2 ratios and adjusted p-values. The six proteins at the ±9.97 floor were seen in one condition only and are shown as present or absent.
datasets.reproduction: The headline claim is right, but the statistic behind it cannot be used: the −9.97 value for IER3IP1 is a floor shared by six proteins seen only in wild type.
caveats: Labelling depends on access to the ER lumen as well as on abundance, so changes are not directly comparable with whole-cell datasets.

datasets.title: EMC2 promotes triple negative breast cancer growth by protecting FDFT1 from endoplasmic reticulum associated degradation to impair ferroptosis susceptibility
datasets.reanalysis: log2 of shEMC2 over control abundance, median-centred over the 935 proteins seen in both samples. Proteins seen in one sample only are shown as present or absent, not imputed.
datasets.reproduction: The main claim holds: FDFT1 is down 3.29 log2, as reported. TFRC is up (+0.95).
caveats: Unreplicated, so single-protein values are noisy; some nuclear RNA-binding proteins fall more than 8-fold.
EMC2 itself and the other EMC subunits were not detected, so neither the knockdown nor the state of the complex can be checked from these data.

datasets.title: Disrupted ER membrane protein complex–mediated topogenesis drives congenital neural crest defects
datasets.replicates: Three morpholino and three control samples
datasets.reanalysis: log2 of the mean normalised abundance, morpholino over control, with the authors’ ANOVA p and q values. Every accession in a protein group is matched; obsolete accessions were traced through UniProt and UniParc.
datasets.reproduction: Partly reproduces. The proteins behind the paper’s WNT, integrin and cadherin pathway calls are lower at the authors’ unadjusted threshold (ANOVA p < 0.05), but the changes are small and none survives correction for multiple testing: β-catenin (ctnnb1) is 1.2-fold lower (−0.27 log2, p = 0.026, q = 0.71), and of 173 proteins at p < 0.05 only two (sp1 and agr2) have q < 0.05. Fzd2 is lower (−0.45) but not significant, as the paper states. Membrane proteins are not over-represented among the decreased proteins (7 of 70 proteins at least 1.5-fold lower, against 264 of 2,514 overall), and multi-pass proteins are not lower than soluble proteins (median log2 change −0.03 against −0.06).
caveats: Whole embryos at stage 24: only about one protein in ten detected is a membrane protein, so the experiment has little power to see membrane-protein loss.
Only about half of the deposited accessions are still current in UniProt. 209 protein groups carry retired gene-model identifiers with no current entry and have no membrane call or orthologue.
emc1 itself was not detected; four other subunits were, with a median of −0.52 and emc7 at −1.00 (complex altered), although none of these changes is significant.

datasets.title: Structure of the ER membrane complex, a transmembrane-domain insertase
datasets.perturbation: emc3, emc4 and emc6 deletion strains
datasets.fraction: DDM extract of membranes, not whole cells
datasets.reanalysis: Difference of the authors’ log2 median-normalised intensities, deletion minus wild type.
datasets.reproduction: A ranked list only, without replicates: 32, 58 and 81 proteins fall more than 2-fold in emc3Δ, emc4Δ and emc6Δ. The paper reports 38 membrane proteins as significantly reduced using its own pipeline.
caveats: emc6Δ loses the complex (other subunits median −1.31). In emc3Δ Emc4 falls 2.13 log2, and in emc4Δ Emc4 is gone, so both are altered without the whole complex falling.

datasets.title: The endoplasmic reticulum membrane protein complex localizes to the mitochondrial-endoplasmic reticulum interface and its subunits modulate phospholipid biosynthesis in Trypanosoma brucei
datasets.perturbation: TbEMC3 and TbEMC8 knockdown by RNAi, harvested at 3 and 3.5 days
datasets.replicates: Three SILAC replicates (label swap) per condition
datasets.reanalysis: Mean log2 ratio (induced over uninduced) and p-value as given by the authors.
datasets.reproduction: Holds: the Kennedy-pathway enzymes are unchanged, as the paper states. Few proteins change (2 to 12 per condition at 1.5-fold and p < 0.05).
caveats: TbEMC3 RNAi lowers only TbEMC3; TbEMC8 RNAi also lowers TbEMC3 (−2.44) and TbEMC2 (−1.65) while the other subunits stay flat. The complex is altered in every condition, through loss of TbEMC3, without the whole complex falling.
Fig. 1 of the paper labels TbEMC8 as Tb927.7.1570; the RNAi target in the methods and data is Tb927.8.1570.
Human orthologues for T. brucei include family-level matches; each is marked.
